findings.refutation: The subject authors forty per-D-002-platform copies. $.whatIsAuthored opens 'Forty platform-indexed copies of the ten D-298 catalog members.' $.purpose opens 'Author per-D-002-platform copies of the ten D-298 implementations.' $.authorityClaim says the artifact 'PROPOSES leftover-design per-D-002-platform copies'. $.summary.platformCopiesAuthored is true, $.summary.authoredFiles is 40, $.summary.copyCount is 40, $.authoredCatalog.copyCount is 40, and each of the ten members carries a four-entry platformCopies array. Forty files exist on disk under docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g20.v6/ at mode 0444, byte-identical to their payloads. The clause is carried verbatim from g20-fixture-corpus.v5, where it was true.
findings.whyItIsAFinding: This is the 'claims contradicted by the bytes' class in its purest form: a flat, unqualified denial in the artifact's own voice of the single thing the artifact exists to do. A doesNot list is load-bearing - it is what a later remasurement reads to establish what the recorded artifact did not do. Recording this text would put a false negative claim into the record about the very act being recorded.
findings.repairShape: Delete $.doesNot[15], or restate it as the boundary that is actually true, e.g. 'Does not author a fifth platform copy or a Windows copy.' whatIsNotAuthored[9] already carries that true boundary, so deletion is sufficient.

findings.claim: "per-platform copies are claimed authored by g20-fixture-corpus.v6"
findings.refutation: The subject claims exactly this, in six places: whatIsAuthored, purpose, authorityClaim, registerRowNote, summary.platformCopiesAuthored true, and authoredCatalog.members[*].platformCopies. In g20-fixture-corpus.v5 this entry read 'per-platform copies are claimed authored by g20-fixture-corpus.v5' and was a correct guard, because v5 authored none. The v5-to-v6 token swap turned a satisfied guard into a self-refutation: by the candidate's own stated failure condition, the candidate fails.
findings.whyItIsAFinding: A failsIf entry is the artifact's own acceptance predicate. An artifact that satisfies one of its own failsIf conditions cannot be accepted on its own terms, independently of any external judgement. This is strictly worse than M-1: M-1 is a false statement, M-2 is a self-declared failure.
findings.repairShape: Delete $.failsIf[25], or invert it to the guard that now matters, e.g. 'a platform copy digest is unequal to its fixtures/g20.v2/ payload' or 'a fifth platform copy is authored'. failsIf[16] and failsIf[17] already guard the Windows and invented-list attacks.
